verification.policy: A status of 'verified' means the behavior was checked, not that it looked right while somebody was reading the code. So an entry carries 'verified_on': for each platform LinSCP ships on, the suites whose tests cover it. LinSCP ships on Linux alone - the Windows port was removed - so an entry may be 'verified' only when 'linux' appears in that map naming the suites that actually ran it. The rule is still written for any number of platforms, and a suite that is not listed under a platform cannot be cited for it, because evidence nobody can reproduce is not evidence. The notes stay authoritative about what is missing either way - evidence for the parts that are covered does not certify the rest, which is why --require-full fails while any entry is not verified.

linux.how: make -C source/linux all check && make -C source/linux check-live (the same suites also run under CMake/CTest: cmake -S . -B build && cmake --build build && ctest --test-dir build); dpkg-buildpackage -b -us -uc builds the .deb that CI installs; `make -C source/linux check-live` includes the browser upload regression suite

suites.unit: source/linux/tests/UnitTest.cpp - 967 checks of the parts that need no I/O: permission and mode parsing, masks, path handling, the transfer and synchronization planners (every word and list '-criteria=' takes, the ones it refuses, and a plan refused over a file nobody could hash), the proxy session settings, parameter and timestamp expansion, the stored-session file, the file-hash and HMAC helpers, and AWS Signature Version 4 signing (canonical request, derived signing key and Authorization header, pinned against botocore's vectors).
suites.script:
source/linux/tests/ScriptTest.py - the command line and script semantics against no server: abbreviations, switches, batch modes and exit codes, local listings, help, -log and -xmllog, and stored-session password encryption (a 'savesession -password' value
written as 'lscp1$' ciphertext under sessions.key and preserved across a
re-save without the key file). The transfer presets are checked here too: the savepreset/option preset/rmspreset lifecycle, a preset stored with a site and restored when it opens, -permissions on downloads, and -rawtransfersettings validation. So are the synchronization criteria (every word and list '-criteria=' takes, the values it refuses with the names it accepts, and the two the 'both' direction cannot honour) and the raw proxy settings of 'open' and 'savesession': each upstream name applied, an unknown one refused, an incomplete or unusable proxy refused, and the password masked in the echo and in the action log.
suites.live-sftp:
source/linux/tests/LiveSftpTest.py against source/linux/tests/TestSftpServer.py - refused opens (wrong password, unexpected host key), operations the server denies, an interrupted download kept in '.filepart' and its resume (automatic and with -resume), the same for an interrupted upload, a continuation that must not splice an existing destination, a stale oversized staging file, resuming across a connection that died, option resume off disabling staging, and timestamps in both directions, a synchronization whose '-criteria=checksum' sees a change the timestamp and the size hide and brings the local copy back in line, sessions carried by a SOCKS5 proxy with and without credentials (TestProxyServer.py, a wrong password refused by the proxy rather than worked around) and a stored site that keeps its proxy, and the shared stored-password format (a password encrypted by the GUI
module opening a stored session, a missing key file reported without losing
the value, and a core-written password decrypted by the GUI's reader). Recursive directory copy and multiple source files into an existing destination directory are tested over SFTP; the test server refuses the optional copy-data extension, so these prove the streamed fallback rather than the native extension. A second server mode implements copy-data and verifies the native extension path as well as exact copied bytes. The server can also refuse check-file-name, which proves the download-and-hash fallback for sha-256, sha-1, md5 and crc32, or implement the extension, which proves the native sha-256 digest and that the client does not fall back after a valid reply. It also proves that synchronize remote with a path exclusion ('-filemask=|skip/') leaves an excluded file untouched despite -delete and does not upload files from the excluded subtree. Recursive symbolic chmod is checked over a nested tree, including exact directory and file modes. copyid installs a generated OpenSSH public key into the test SFTP home, verifies the 0700/0600 permissions and proves that repeating the command does not duplicate the key.
suites.live-s3: source/linux/tests/LiveS3Test.py against source/linux/tests/TestS3Server.py - a throwaway S3 endpoint over TLS (the fixtures are committed) that re-derives every SigV4 signature with its own hmac/hashlib code: missing and wrong credentials refused, bucket/object CRUD, resumed downloads using HTTP byte ranges, CopyObject for cp and rename, and a 20 MiB+123 upload checked as multipart initiation, three parts with returned ETags, completion, exact roundtrip checksum and no leftover upload. Synthetic HTTP-200 Error documents exercise CopyObject and multipart completion parsing, including abort cleanup after completion fails. The server also accepts a botocore-signed reference request. The client reaches it with curl over TLS on 127.0.0.1.
suites.gui: source/gui/tests/ClientTest.js under node with jsdom - the real Commander page booted against a stubbed backend: rendering, selection, the editor, synchronization preview and run, filename and full-text search controls/results, the site manager, terminal, queue, host-key verification, synchronized browsing (the counterpart probe, following and refusing when the other side has no such folder) and drag and drop between the panes (payload, drop-target highlight, queued upload with the dragged names, same-pane drop ignored).
suites.live-dav: source/linux/tests/LiveDavTest.py against source/linux/tests/TestDavServer.py - a throwaway WebDAV endpoint over plain HTTP with Basic challenge authentication: PROPFIND listings, stat with real size/time/missing-path handling, mkdir/rmdir/MOVE/DELETE, and upload/download; single-file cp uses COPY with an absolute Destination and Overwrite header, verified by a server-side operation counter and an exact readback while the source remains; a 405 refusal also verifies the streamed fallback byte-for-byte. It also checks upstream-shaped console output, aliases and transfer presets. keepuptodate uploads local files to the remote side, and a nested file arrival wakes the inotify watcher rather than waiting for the 30-second rescan. The suite is standard-library-only and needs nothing but curl.
suites.manual: Hand-run against the same server, kept here because no automated test does it yet: 'chmod -recursive' octal and symbolic over a tree, 'copyid' with an OpenSSH .pub and with a private key, 'put -append', 'get -append', -resumesupport=64 across a partial file, -speed=40, -preservetime=all on a directory, -xmllog= with -parameter. Reproduce with source/linux/build/linuxscp -batch -hostkey='*' -command="open sftp://testuser:testpass@127.0.0.1:12765/ ; ..." after starting the server.
suites.gui-search: source/gui/tests/RemoteSearchTest.py - backend tests with a fake session covering literal UTF-8 content search, case sensitivity, filename-mask filtering, binary/non-UTF-8 and oversized-file skips, and scan-budget enforcement. The jsdom ClientTest.js also checks the GUI toggle, request payload, bounded-search summary and escaped result snippet.
suites.gui-browser-upload: source/gui/tests/BrowserUploadTest.py - exercises the authenticated HTTP upload endpoint, rejects a request without the run token, stages exact binary bytes into a private temporary file, queues the exact remote destination with progress metadata, and removes partial staging files when a request ends early. ClientTest.js checks the desktop drag/drop payload and target.
suites.gui-desktop-uri: source/gui/tests/DesktopUriTest.py - validates sftp://, ftp:// and ftps:// desktop URLs, default and explicit ports, escaped credentials and paths, IPv6 authorities, rejected malformed/query URLs, and startup creation/activation of the site tab without trusting an unknown host key.

!.notes: Runs the command over SSH exec in a one-shot second connection and prints its output, like upstream 'call'. No interactive shell with a pty.

ascii.notes: Sets 'option transfer ascii' like upstream, with arity checks; the conversion is applied by get/put/synchronize and was verified byte-exact against a live server. Transfer presets apply to this command - by 'option preset name', by 'savesession -preset=' when the site opens, and by the host/user/directory/mask rules when no preset was picked - with the command's own switches always winning, covered by the script suite and by an ascii preset converting a live upload.

binary.notes: Sets 'option transfer binary' like upstream, with arity checks. Transfer presets apply to this command - by 'option preset name', by 'savesession -preset=' when the site opens, and by the host/user/directory/mask rules when no preset was picked - with the command's own switches always winning, covered by the script suite and by an ascii preset converting a live upload.

bye.notes: Stops the script where it stands with no output and no arguments, like upstream's continue flag (exit, quit and end are the same command, bye an alias of exit). Covered by the script suite.

call.notes: Rejoins and re-quotes the arguments and runs them over SSH exec in a one-shot second connection (the main SFTP session stays open). No interactive shell with a pty.

cd.notes: With no argument it goes to the home directory captured at connect time; either form prints the resulting directory, like upstream (upstream's script interpreter has no directory history either). Covered by the live WebDAV suite.

checksum.notes: For the four documented algorithms (sha-256, sha-1, md5, crc32), returns the lowercase digest and remote path. On SFTP it asks the check-file-name extension first for supported algorithms and falls back to downloading and hashing when the server declines; covered by live-sftp for all four fallback digests and the native sha-256 reply.

chmod.notes: Octal and symbolic modes ('u+x', 'a=r,go-w', 'u+s', 'X') and -recursive over a directory tree, symbolic links skipped; the mode is checked before the connection so a typo is reported even when offline. Upstream's script command passes an octal string only, so the symbolic forms and recursion are an extension; recursive symbolic 'g+w' is verified live across nested directories and files against a server that implements SETSTAT. Missing: owner and group changes, and upstream's per-site permission defaults.

close.notes: Closes the session with no argument or with the 1-based index of the session to close ('close 1' is the only index that exists here), prints "Session '<name>' closed." like upstream, and refuses other indexes; like upstream it needs a connection before the argument is even looked at. Opening a different stored site closes the previous connection the same way. Covered by the script suite (offline refusal) and the live WebDAV suite.

copyid.notes: Reads the session's private key (or the given key file: an OpenSSH public key, an OpenSSH private key or a PuTTY .ppk, foreign formats imported through the bundled PuTTY core) and appends its authorized_keys line to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, creating the directory 0700 and the file 0600 and leaving an already installed key alone. Needs an sftp:// or scp:// session; an encrypted key asks for its passphrase in an interactive session and is refused in batch mode. Covered by live-sftp with a generated .pub file, exact ~/.ssh and authorized_keys permissions, and duplicate suppression; the manual evidence additionally checks a PEM private key; the upstream command takes exactly one argument, ours also accepts none.

cp.notes: Remote copy is checked through native SFTP copy-data when the server implements it, streamed SFTP fallback when it does not, WebDAV COPY (and streamed fallback on refusal), and S3 CopyObject. Recursive trees, multiple sources into an existing directory, overwrite refusal in batch mode, and explicit overwrite with confirm off are covered by the live-sftp, live-dav and live-s3 suites.

dir.notes: Alias of 'ls' with the same listing, mask and no-match semantics. Covered by the live WebDAV suite.

echo.notes: Plain token output. The line has already been through the upstream expansions - script parameters, %TIMESTAMP% and environment variables - because they are applied before dispatch; text in single quotes is left alone. Covered by the script suite.

exit.notes: Stops the script where it stands with no output and no arguments, like upstream's continue flag. Covered by the script suite.

get.notes: Binary/ASCII/automatic transfers with full WinSCP file masks (name, directory and path masks, size/time criteria), -filemask=, option include/exclude, failonnomatch, resume (binary only, rejected with ASCII), -resumesupport=on|off|<KB>, -append (native SFTP only), -speed=<KB/s>, -neweronly/-noneweronly and -preservetime[=all]. Speed, append, resume and the time preservation were verified against a live SFTP server. Transfer presets apply (see 'option'), '-permissions[=mode]' gives the downloaded file that local mode - the =mode form checked on a live server, the valueless form taking the remote file's mode when the server reports one (parse-checked) - and '-rawtransfersettings[=N]' accepts upstream's key=value vocabulary with a refused-by-name error for every setting this build does not apply, the TransferMode conversion exercised live - the preset and raw-setting parts covered by the script suite and a live WebDAV transfer. Resume-capable transfers stage through upstream's '.filepart' name and are moved onto the destination only when complete, so an interrupted transfer never leaves a truncated file under the final name; a continuation reads the staging file only, never splices the existing destination, and 'option resume automatic' (the default) stages binary files from upstream's 100 KB threshold, 'on' stages everything and 'off' nothing; all three behaviors are exercised against a live SFTP server.

help.notes: 'help' lists every command as upstream does, name in an 8-wide column followed by its one-line description; 'help <command>' prints that command's help text, and aliases resolve to the command they stand for (unknown names are refused). Covered by the script suite.

keepuptodate.notes: Takes no direction word; like upstream it reflects changes in the local directory onto the remote one. Accepts -delete, -filemask=, -transfer=, -interval=, -count= and -continue (keeps watching after a failed pass). A recursive inotify watcher starts another pass on local changes; -interval= remains a full-rescan safety net, with timer polling if the watch cannot be set up. It runs in the foreground until Ctrl-C or -count= passes complete (batch mode requires -count=). The live WebDAV suite passes the local-to-remote direction and the watcher assertion; broader synchronization gaps listed below remain. Resume-capable transfers stage through upstream's '.filepart' name and are moved onto the destination only when complete, so an interrupted transfer never leaves a truncated file under the final name; a continuation reads the staging file only, never splices the existing destination, and 'option resume automatic' (the default) stages binary files from upstream's 100 KB threshold, 'on' stages everything and 'off' nothing; all three behaviors are exercised against a live SFTP server.

lcd.notes: Changes the local directory and prints the directory it landed in, like upstream; a directory that cannot be entered is an error and stops a batch script. Covered by the script suite.

lls.notes: Upstream's columns: date, time, size (or <DIR> for a directory) and the name, with the date and time widths fitted to the widest entry; a trailing wildcard leaf masks the listing, the default lists everything, and a path that matches nothing prints the no-match sentence - a failure only under option failonnomatch. Covered by the script suite.

ln.notes: SFTP SYMLINK with the upstream argument order (target, link), verified live. Fails explicitly on protocols without symlinks.

lpwd.notes: Prints the local working directory, no arguments like upstream. Covered by the script suite.

ls.notes: Listing whose mask comes from the trailing path component ('ls docs/*.log'), like upstream. Long format prints the entry's listing line - the server's long name over SFTP, a synthesized ls -l line on the transfer backends - which is what upstream prints as well (File->ListingStr). A mask that matches nothing prints the no-match sentence, a failure only under option failonnomatch. Covered by the live WebDAV and S3 suites.

man.notes: Same as 'help': the two-column listing without arguments, the per-command help text with one, aliases resolving to their command. Covered by the script suite.

mget.notes: Same implementation as 'get', including its -speed=, -append and -resumesupport= switches. Transfer presets of the implementation this alias shares apply (by name, with the site, or by rule), covered by the preset tests of the script and live WebDAV suites. Resume-capable transfers stage through upstream's '.filepart' name and are moved onto the destination only when complete, so an interrupted transfer never leaves a truncated file under the final name; a continuation reads the staging file only, never splices the existing destination, and 'option resume automatic' (the default) stages binary files from upstream's 100 KB threshold, 'on' stages everything and 'off' nothing; all three behaviors are exercised against a live SFTP server.

mkdir.notes: Creates exactly one directory - one argument like upstream - and is silent on success; refusals (a name that exists) and other server answers are reported and fail the script. Covered by the live WebDAV and S3 suites.

mput.notes: Same implementation as 'put', including its -speed=, -append and -resumesupport= switches. Transfer presets of the implementation this alias shares apply (by name, with the site, or by rule), covered by the preset tests of the script and live WebDAV suites. Resume-capable transfers stage through upstream's '.filepart' name and are moved onto the destination only when complete, so an interrupted transfer never leaves a truncated file under the final name; a continuation reads the staging file only, never splices the existing destination, and 'option resume automatic' (the default) stages binary files from upstream's 100 KB threshold, 'on' stages everything and 'off' nothing; all three behaviors are exercised against a live SFTP server.

mv.notes: Multi-source with an existing-directory target, rename in place and confirm-on-overwrite, like upstream. Covered by the live WebDAV suite.

open.notes:
URL sessions and stored-session names; an unknown host key is refused and reported on a HOSTKEY line so it can be pinned. '-rawsettings[=N] NAME=VALUE...' applies upstream's proxy session settings (ProxyMethod, ProxyHost, ProxyPort, ProxyUsername, ProxyPassword, ProxyTelnetCommand, ProxyLocalCommand, ProxyDNS, ProxyLocalhost, ProxyExcludeList) and refuses by name any setting this build does not apply, an incomplete proxy, and a proxy the curl transports cannot run; the switches of 'open' also apply to a stored site, as they do upstream. Missing: SSH tunnels, session folders, session selection UI, and the raw settings beyond the proxy ones. A stored password that cannot be decrypted is reported and the
open continues without it.

option.notes: echo, batch (on/off/abort/continue), confirm, resume, transfer (binary/ascii/automatic), include/exclude (one mask, setting either clears the other, 'clear' resets), synchdelete, failonnomatch, reconnecttime (seconds or off, with automatic reconnect), editor, editmaxsize, and a listing when called with no name. Option and value names may be abbreviated when the abbreviation is unambiguous; masks, programs and numbers are never abbreviated. 'option preset <name>' selects a transfer preset for the following transfers, 'option preset off' disables presets for the session and a missing preset name fails loudly; 'savesession -preset=' persists the preset with the site, which loads it when opened, both directions covered by the script suite and the live WebDAV preset roundtrip.

put.notes: Binary/ASCII/automatic transfers with WinSCP file masks, -filemask=, option include/exclude, failonnomatch, -permissions=/-nopermissions, and the -resume, -append, -speed=, -resumesupport=, -neweronly/-noneweronly and -preservetime[=all] switches of 'get' (append and resume are mutually exclusive and need the native SFTP transport). Verified against a live server. Transfer presets apply (see 'option') and '-rawtransfersettings[=N]' understands upstream's key=value settings, refused by name when this build cannot apply them; a preset-driven ascii upload and a raw TransferMode upload were both checked against a live server. Setting permissions on the server itself needs the native SFTP transport, so -permissions on uploads stays parse-checked where curl cannot chmod; the preset and raw-setting parts are covered by the script and live WebDAV suites. Resume-capable transfers stage through upstream's '.filepart' name and are moved onto the destination only when complete, so an interrupted transfer never leaves a truncated file under the final name; a continuation reads the staging file only, never splices the existing destination, and 'option resume automatic' (the default) stages binary files from upstream's 100 KB threshold, 'on' stages everything and 'off' nothing; all three behaviors are exercised against a live SFTP server.

pwd.notes: Prints the remote working directory after checking there is a session, like upstream. Covered by the live WebDAV suite.

recv.notes: Same implementation as 'get', including its -speed=, -append and -resumesupport= switches. Transfer presets of the implementation this alias shares apply (by name, with the site, or by rule), covered by the preset tests of the script and live WebDAV suites. Resume-capable transfers stage through upstream's '.filepart' name and are moved onto the destination only when complete, so an interrupted transfer never leaves a truncated file under the final name; a continuation reads the staging file only, never splices the existing destination, and 'option resume automatic' (the default) stages binary files from upstream's 100 KB threshold, 'on' stages everything and 'off' nothing; all three behaviors are exercised against a live SFTP server.

rename.notes: One source and one destination only, like upstream's mv in its rename form. Covered by the live WebDAV suite.

rm.notes: Multiple files, masks and -onlyfile (directories are skipped with a status), no-match reporting gated by option failonnomatch, like upstream. No recursive delete, matching upstream. Covered by the live WebDAV suite.

rmdir.notes: Multiple directories in one command, continuing past failures; only empty directories, like upstream. Covered by the live WebDAV suite.

send.notes: Same implementation as 'put', including its -speed=, -append and -resumesupport= switches. Transfer presets of the implementation this alias shares apply (by name, with the site, or by rule), covered by the preset tests of the script and live WebDAV suites. Resume-capable transfers stage through upstream's '.filepart' name and are moved onto the destination only when complete, so an interrupted transfer never leaves a truncated file under the final name; a continuation reads the staging file only, never splices the existing destination, and 'option resume automatic' (the default) stages binary files from upstream's 100 KB threshold, 'on' stages everything and 'off' nothing; all three behaviors are exercised against a live SFTP server.

session.notes: Upstream 'session' semantics: it needs an open session, no argument lists the open sessions as '%3d name' and prints which one is active, and 'session <index>' switches (only index 1 exists with one connection; other indexes are refused). The stored-sites listing, export/import and lookup by name moved to the plural 'sessions' command, which savesession/rmsession feed and 'open <name>' also resolves. The session folder tree and raw settings are not part of this command and stay tracked under 'open'. Covered by the script suite (the offline refusals) and the live WebDAV suite (listing, switching).

stat.notes: Prints the one listing line upstream prints for the path (the line 'ls -l' shows: permissions, links, owner, group, size, time and name), exactly one line with no key/value text. The breakdown this used to print lives on as the LinSCP addition 'attr', which the graphical client parses instead. Covered by the live WebDAV and S3 suites.

symlink.notes: Alias of 'ln': SFTP SYMLINK with the upstream argument order (target, link). Fails explicitly on protocols without symlinks.

synchronize.notes: Planner with direction, -criteria= (upstream's 'none', 'either' and 'both', or a comma-separated list of 'time', 'size' and 'checksum'; 'checksum' compares the contents through SHA-256, computed by the server when the transport can and from a downloaded copy otherwise, and a file that cannot be hashed stops the plan instead of counting as equal), -filemask=, -delete/-nodelete (default from option synchdelete), -mirror (rejects 'both', resolves any difference toward the source), -transfer=binary|ascii|automatic, -preview, -nonrecursive, -interval=, -count=; 'both' keeps a state record and decides from it, so it refuses the criteria it could not honour ('checksum' and 'none') rather than ignoring them the way upstream does. Verified live. The path exclusion '-filemask=|skip/' is checked live: it prunes that subtree and protects an excluded destination file from '-delete'. Missing: upstream's richer conflict-resolution UI and some state/metadata cases. Resume-capable transfers stage through upstream's '.filepart' name and are moved onto the destination only when complete, so an interrupted transfer never leaves a truncated file under the final name; a continuation reads the staging file only, never splices the existing destination, and 'option resume automatic' (the default) stages binary files from upstream's 100 KB threshold, 'on' stages everything and 'off' nothing; all three behaviors are exercised against a live SFTP server.

features.name: SFTP
features.notes: Native PuTTY transport rather than a curl session. SYMLINK, copy-data (with a streamed fallback) and check-file-name (with a local hash fallback) are implemented and were verified against a live in-process SFTP server; unknown extensions still fail explicitly rather than being ignored. The native check-file-name reply is covered by the extension-enabled live test server; metadata policies remain.

features.name: SCP
features.notes: Delegated to curl, whose SCP support depends on its build; no WinSCP shell-based directory and command engine.

features.name: FTP/FTPS
features.notes: curl transport and listing parser; no full upstream MLSD, TLS configuration, active/passive and server compatibility validation.

features.name: WebDAV
features.notes: PROPFIND-driven filesystem: Depth 0/1 listings parsed from the 207 multi-status whatever namespace prefix the server chose (resourcetype, getcontentlength, getlastmodified), stat through Depth 0 with real sizes, times and a missing path that reports as missing, MKCOL with named exists/parent-refusal messages, MOVE with an absolute-URI Destination and Overwrite semantics, single-file COPY with absolute Destination/Overwrite for cp, and a streamed fallback when COPY is refused; DELETE with 409 read as 'not empty' - and rmdir checking children first, because a DAV collection DELETE is recursive by specification. 'open' probes with PROPFIND and refuses a 401 after the --anyauth challenge round-trip (which also serves digest-only servers) and a 405 that means the server is not DAV at all. The live server-side COPY path is asserted by the mock's method counter. Missing: LOCK/UNLOCK, dead properties, collection-level precondition handling and If-header preconditions.

features.name: Amazon S3
features.notes: AWS Signature Version 4 signing over curl (AWS4-HMAC-SHA256, pinned to botocore's vectors in the unit suite), s3:// session URLs with region from AWS_REGION, AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, the hostname (s3.<region>.amazonaws.com or .com.cn) or us-east-1, and path-style bucket access: ListBuckets, ListObjectsV2 with delimiter and continuation, HEAD stat, get with range resume and Last-Modified preservation, PutObject for small objects, multipart uploads for files over 16 MiB (8 MiB minimum parts, scaled to stay within 10,000 parts), directory markers with bucket-aware mkdir/rmdir, CopyObject for cp and copy-plus-delete for rename (multipart copy is not implemented), and explicit refusal of unsigned or wrongly signed requests. On a handled failure the client attempts to abort the multipart upload; interrupted uploads restart from the first part and are not resumable. The live TLS mock re-derives signatures and checks multipart initiation, parts, ETags, completion, CopyObject, embedded HTTP-200 Error bodies, and abort cleanup. Not implemented: ACLs, versioning, storage classes, SSE options and object metadata beyond content.

features.name: Transfers
features.notes: Binary and ASCII/automatic transfers with full WinSCP file masks (name, directory and path masks plus size/time criteria), include/exclude options, failonnomatch, resume with a -resumesupport= threshold (binary only), -append to add to an existing file, -speed= bandwidth limiting (pacing in the native engine, curl --limit-rate elsewhere), -preservetime with -preservetime=all for directories, and reconnecttime with automatic reconnect; ASCII conversion, speed, append, resume and times were verified byte-exact or by timing against a live server. Resume-capable transfers stage through upstream's '.filepart' temporary and are renamed into place only when complete ('option resume automatic|on|off', default automatic = upstream's rsSmart at 100 KB), which the live suite checks for both directions, for interruption and restart, for a stale oversized staging file and against splicing an existing destination. Transfer presets (named, per-site and rule-based, using upstream's copy-parameter vocabulary) drive these transfers too, checked live. S3 multipart uploads report progress between completed parts; generic curl transfers still lack in-flight per-file progress. Interrupted S3 multipart uploads restart from part one rather than resuming remote upload IDs.

features.name: Synchronization
features.notes: Planner with direction, -criteria= (upstream's 'none', 'either' and 'both', or a list of 'time', 'size' and 'checksum'), -filemask=, -delete/-nodelete (option synchdelete as the default), -mirror (any difference resolves toward the source; rejected with 'both'), -transfer=binary|ascii|automatic applied to planned transfers, -preview, -nonrecursive, -interval=, -count= and keepuptodate -continue; 'both' keeps a state record to tell changes from conflicts and refuses the criteria that record cannot honour ('checksum', 'none'). '-criteria=checksum' reads both files - the server's checksum when the transport can ask for it, a downloaded copy otherwise - and a file that cannot be hashed refuses the plan instead of passing for equal; verified live against a server without the extension. Verified live. A recursive inotify watcher provides keepuptodate's local-change notification, whose local-to-remote direction and watcher assertion the live WebDAV suite passes. The path exclusion '-filemask=|skip/' prunes a subtree and protects an excluded remote file from '-delete', verified live against SFTP. Missing: upstream's conflict resolution UI; planned transfers stage through '.filepart' like get/put when the resume setting and the transfer mode allow it.

features.name: Sessions/configuration
features.notes:
sessions.ini site manager shared by the console and the graphical client: session, savesession, rmsession, 'open <name>', export/import, last-used tracking, and the transfer preset a site stores with '-preset=' and loads when it opens. Stored passwords are encrypted under a sibling 'sessions.key' (created
on first use, user-only access) in a format the graphical client reads and
writes too. A proxy travels with a site: 'open -rawsettings' applies upstream's proxy settings, 'savesession -rawsettings' stores them with the proxy password encrypted like a session password, and a site whose stored proxy cannot be decrypted is refused rather than opened without it. Missing: folder tree, the raw settings beyond the proxy ones, and the full upstream
configuration model.

features.name: Security/authentication
features.notes:
Password, private-key and ssh-agent authentication and the host-key policy exist; an unknown or changed key is refused and reported instead of being accepted. GSSAPI is compiled out, and SSH tunnels and curl fingerprint equivalence are incomplete. Proxy configuration is in place under upstream's setting names - SOCKS 4 and 5, HTTP CONNECT, a telnet command or a local command through the PuTTY core, with its DNS, localhost and exclude-list policy - and the curl protocols translate the same settings to --proxy/--proxy-user/--noproxy, refusing a telnet or local-command proxy they cannot run; a proxy password is masked in the echo and in the action log. The curl path honors ProxyLocalhost=0 by adding localhost, 127.0.0.0/8 and ::1/128 to --noproxy; ProxyLocalhost=1 leaves loopback destinations eligible for proxying. The graphical interface now verifies by default, pins on request and stores a pin rather than a wildcard, and its API is bound to loopback behind a per-run token with a Host check; there is still no user account; stored session passwords are encrypted at
rest under sessions.key rather than kept in the clear.

features.name: GUI
features.notes: Browser Commander with one persistent session per tab, dual panes, a transfer queue with progress/pause/cancel/retry, synchronization preview, remote filename and bounded UTF-8 content search, a remote editor, the site manager and host-key pinning, driven by a loopback HTTP API behind a per-run token (Host-checked) over -server. Synchronized browsing (the toggle follows directory changes across both panes, refuses when the counterpart folder is missing, and keeps the pair aligned going up) and drag and drop between the panes (dragged entries carry a payload, the target pane highlights, dropping queues the upload/download with exactly those names, a same-pane drop does nothing) are implemented like WinSCP's Commander, both covered by the jsdom regression test. Dropping individual files from the operating system's file manager onto the remote pane now queues authenticated, bounded uploads through the task queue (jsdom and BrowserUploadTest.py); folders and drops onto the local pane remain unsupported. Still not upstream Commander/Explorer: custom commands and localization.

features.name: Editing/search
features.notes: 'edit' downloads, runs the configured editor and uploads on change, with a size limit and a refusal when the remote file changed meanwhile; GUI remote search matches filename masks recursively or searches literal UTF-8 content inside files matching the mask. Content search caps each file at 8 MiB, each search at 200 files/64 MiB, and reports skipped and truncated results; binary, non-UTF-8 and oversized files are skipped. Missing: save/upload monitoring of local edits, broader encoding handling and the custom command system.

features.name: Automation
features.notes: Console scripting with WinSCP switches, unambiguous command and option abbreviations, script parameters (%1%..%9% via -parameter), %TIMESTAMP% with relative offsets and formats, %NAME% environment expansion, and an XML action log (-xmllog=) recording every command, result, message and transfer with passwords masked. Missing: the WinSCP .NET assembly and PowerShell APIs, and equivalence with upstream's log format, which our log mirrors in structure but does not copy; the expansions are not applied to -server input, where the graphical client quotes literal paths.

features.name: Desktop integration
features.notes: The Debian desktop entry registers sftp://, ftp:// and ftps://; the GUI launcher parses those URLs, connects the requested site in a background tab, preserves the remote directory, and routes an unknown host key into the normal verification UI. URL parsing and tab startup are covered by gui-desktop-uri. Still missing: full OS drag-and-drop of folders, shell integration and extension system.

features.name: Localization/accessibility
features.notes: No equivalent upstream translation catalog and desktop accessibility verification.

features.name: Packaging/platforms
features.notes: Linux is the only platform this client is built, packaged and tested on: the Makefile build, the CMake/CTest build and the Debian package all run in CI, which installs the .deb and starts the console and graphical clients from the installed paths. The Windows port that used to sit beside them was removed, so no claim in this inventory rests on a second platform. A build that passes does not establish functional parity.

linuxscp_additions.name: edit
linuxscp_additions.notes: Downloads the remote file, runs $LINUXSCP_EDITOR/$EDITOR or option editor, and uploads it back when it changed, refusing files over option editmaxsize and refusing to overwrite a file modified since the download. No local-side edit, no editor fallback chain or encoding handling beyond the installed editor. Upstream's script interpreter has no 'edit' command at the pinned commit, so this is a LinSCP command rather than parity work.

linuxscp_additions.name: savesession / rmsession
linuxscp_additions.notes: Store and forget a named site in sessions.ini, which 'open <name>' and the graphical site manager then resolve. Upstream has no such script commands; it edits the configuration through its GUI and the .NET assembly. The password given with -password is encrypted under sessions.key on save, '-rawsettings' stores the proxy settings with the site the same way - its password encrypted under the same key file, kept byte for byte across a re-save this machine cannot decrypt, dropped with the credential when ProxyMethod=None clears the proxy, and refused at open when the key file is gone rather than connected around - and a stored value that cannot be decrypted is preserved across an unrelated re-save. Covered by the script suite.

linuxscp_additions.name: sessions
linuxscp_additions.notes: Stored-sites companion of 'session': lists the sites in sessions.ini with their URL and remote directory, opens one by name (as does 'open <name>'), and exports or imports the whole list (sessions export/import). Not an upstream command name - upstream keeps none of this in its script language - while 'session' itself now follows upstream's open-session semantics. Covered by the script suite.

linuxscp_additions.name: show
linuxscp_additions.notes: Recognised and answered with the reason: this build connects with the SFTP subsystem, so there is no shell state to show, and the command says so instead of failing as an unknown name. Not an upstream script command. Covered by the script suite.

linuxscp_additions.name: del, md, sync, quit, end
linuxscp_additions.notes: Extra aliases accepted for convenience (rm, mkdir, synchronize, exit, exit). Upstream registers 'dir' but not these, so they are not counted as upstream coverage. Covered by the script suite (sync, quit, end) and the live WebDAV suite (md, del).

linuxscp_additions.name: attr
linuxscp_additions.notes: The key/value attribute block the console printed before 'stat' followed upstream: path, size, permissions, modified time, SizeBytes, ModifiedEpoch and owner lines, parsed by the graphical client (remote_stat). Not an upstream command - upstream's 'stat' prints the single listing line instead. Covered by the live WebDAV and S3 suites.
